The Passive: The Present Continuous and Present Perfect Tenses

You use the Present Continuous to talk about an action that is happening at the time of speaking. The action or event is in progress.
People are interpreting surrealism in a very personal and subjective manner.

You use the Present Perfect to talk about a finished action or event with present consequences. There is a connection between what happened in the past and the present.
Museums have exhibited Dali's paintings around the world.

You often choose the passive form when you want to talk about an action but are not so interested in saying who or what does/did it. Passives without agents (the doers) are common in biographies.

You can use modals to talk about degrees of certainty and speculate about things in the past.</br> You use them to describe what is definite, probable, possible, or impossible from the speaker's point of view.

You can use must, may, might, and could to describe degrees of certainty.
You can use modals with the Present Perfect to talk about the possibility of a past event that is not clear in the present context.

Example:
Without the surrealist influence, Dali might never have risen to prominence.

images.text: In the early 1920s, a young Salvador Dali met a group of unconventional artists called the Surrealists. These painters, sculptors, and filmmakers took their inspiration from the human mind. In their art, reality is not being represented accurately. Instead it is being interpreted in a very personal and subjective manner. This absence of structure must have appealed greatly to Dali, who quickly became one of the best-known members of the group. Without the surrealist influence, Dali might never have risen to prominence.

Dali's paintings have been exhibited all over the world. His pictures were famous for their grotesque images and strange combinations of objects. At the time, such images may have been quite a shock to the public.

Dali had an extravagant personality and he loved publicity. He was known for his paintings as well as for his bizarre clothing and long, curly moustache. In truth, his unique appearance could have actually contributed to his popularity. Dali continued his artistic work until the end of his life in 1989.

Dali's works have been coveted by art aficionados for years. His avant-garde style and larger-than-life personality still intrigue people today. As a result his works are constantly being bought up by curators and connoisseurs, not to mention amateur aficionados. Buyer beware, though. Copies are being produced by counterfeiters daily. Some fakes have even been spotted with authentic signatures. As always, imitation is the best form of flattery!
